selection.rationale: Gains 10-23 all met the formal full -50..-10 dBm range criterion. Gain 20 was chosen as the engineering compromise: 5.75 dB measured full-scale headroom at -10 dBm and 25.0 dB minimum in-range SNR at -50 dBm, rather than the boundary gain 23 (2.79 dB headroom). No gain outside 10-23 met both the full-range and 2 dB headroom requirements.

notes: All levels pass the gates from 2150 through 2700 MHz.
All levels remain within +/-2 dB from 2150 through 2600 MHz; the -20 and -15 dBm levels also pass at 2650 MHz.
At 2100 MHz a tone is detected with 10-28 dB SNR but the corrected frequency error is about -366 kHz, so the frequency gate fails; the raw peak is not a valid power reading.
No reliable tone is detected at 2000, 2050, or 2750-2950 MHz in this setup.

used_model_start.note: Frequency-only LO/reference correction measured from raw CAP20 bursts. Never applied to the power offset.

used_model_end.note: Frequency-only LO/reference correction measured from raw CAP20 bursts. Never applied to the power offset.

clean_repeat_start.note: Frequency-only LO/reference correction measured from raw CAP20 bursts. Never applied to the power offset.

clean_repeat_end.note: Frequency-only LO/reference correction measured from raw CAP20 bursts. Never applied to the power offset.

lo_calibration.note: The working-band captures used used_model_start. A clean repeat with full per-point metadata was recorded after a tool bug overwrote the first calibration run metadata; the repeat agrees with the end repeat to better than 1 ppm.

recheck_2440_m50.note: The original working-band capture passed all gates but had a 0.486 dB five-block peak-to-peak variation; a repeat at the same setting with fresh source settling was made.

limitations: dBm values are nominal generator level minus the nominal pad; no independent power meter or traceable attenuation calibration was available.
Measured power is integrated CW dBFS in the stated FFT configuration, not a calibrated absolute power or noise figure.
Sensitivity results (phase 2) are setup-limited known-frequency CW detectability, not Wi-Fi BER or thermal-noise-limited receiver sensitivity.
The frequency gate uses a separately measured, frequency-only LO/reference correction; the power offset is never frequency corrected.

phase2_selection.selection_rule: weakest nominal input passing the detection gates; tie-break lowest five-block power standard deviation at that input
phase2_selection.fine_tuning_note: Fine tuning was restricted to the five-index range 63-67 around the coarse candidate 65. An earlier wider refinement attempt was aborted.
phase2_selection.note: Selection was frozen before the sensitivity frequency scans.

sensitivity.note: Thresholds are nominal DUT input; -90 dBm is the weakest tested input. No threshold at -90 means the threshold is at or below the tested floor, not that -90 dBm was proven.

pad_overlap.note: No alignment or correction was fitted. Gains above 50 are compressed at -50 dBm and are not used for the overlap statistic.

raw_adc.note: No exact ADC rail hits occurred in these gain-65 snapshots. High source-off RMS at 2100, 2410, 2450 and 2460 MHz is in-band background/spur energy, not raw ADC clipping in the captured snapshots.

fft_profiles.note: The strongest mirror indicates IQ-image rejection in the captured on-chip spectrum; all reported peaks are at the expected signed baseband position, not an alias.

limitations: All dBm values are nominal generator level minus the nominal 50 dB pad; no independent power meter was available.
Sensitivity is known-frequency CW detectability in this FFT/setup configuration, not Wi-Fi BER, noise figure or thermal-noise-limited sensitivity.
Source-off background and spurs limit several frequencies; the on/off gate is part of the threshold definition.
Thresholds at -90 dBm are at the weakest tested input (the tested floor), not a measured intrinsic limit.
The 10 dB-pad usable-range result is reused from phase 1; -30/-15 dBm cannot be applied through the 50 dB pad because the generator would need +20/+35 dBm.
